title: Verify and source the erythrulose (G+0.693-0.027) interstellar-sugar claims
question: What are the verified facts of the 2026 Nature Astronomy detection of the four-carbon sugar erythrulose toward the molecular cloud G+0.693-0.027 — formation pathway, cloud distance, molecule identity, and whether it is correctly framed as the 'first sugar in the interstellar medium' — so the module's claims can be corrected and cited?
why_now: OriginOfLifeTimeline.tsx, DustGrainExperiment.tsx and learning path CHE-ZUCKER-MOLEKUEL-0001 present the detection as established fact but state a formation pathway (two C2H molecules reacting on a dust grain to C4H8O4) and a distance (450 light-years from the Galactic center) that conflict with the published result (glycolaldehyde + ethylene glycol on cold dust; cloud ~8.2 kpc from Earth, near the Galactic center). EDITORIAL.md rule R-05 requires EP0-EP2 scientific claims to carry a KG/OTA source; this brand-new result (Nature Astronomy, 13 Jul 2026) has none, and the content is republished via the SSF magazine and consumed by NOXIA.
